statement: In an anonymous online survey in 2011 (Global Drug Survey; Winstock & Barratt, 2013), 980 people who had used synthetic cannabis in the past year, almost all of whom also used natural cannabis, rated synthetic cannabis compared with natural cannabis as giving slightly more hangover (mean 3.5 against 2.8 on a 1-10 scale; standardized difference d = 0.22, a small difference), as leaving them less able to function after use (5.5 against 6.9; d = -0.45), with more negative effects while high (d = 0.64), slightly more paranoia (d = 0.27) and much less pleasure (5.0 against 8.6; d = -1.22). Two thirds said a typical smoke of synthetic cannabis left them feeling stoned for about an hour, against two hours or more for natural cannabis in three quarters, and 93% preferred natural cannabis. These are retrospective self-ratings from a self-selected sample recruited through a dance-music magazine and a newspaper, hangover was not defined, the products' contents were unknown, and synthetic cannabinoids sold since 2011 differ. Certainty: very low. Status: single study.
plain: In a 2011 online survey, people who had used both fake (synthetic) cannabis and ordinary cannabis compared them. They said synthetic cannabis gave a slightly worse hangover, made it harder to get on with things afterwards, gave more bad feelings while high and much less enjoyment, and wore off sooner. Most preferred ordinary cannabis. These are people's memories, not tests, and the products sold today are different.
population: People who had used synthetic cannabis in the past year (79.6% men, median age 23, mostly in the US and UK) responding to an online survey in 2011; 99% had also used natural cannabis
exposure: Smoked synthetic cannabis products of unknown content
comparator: The same people's ratings of natural (herbal) cannabis
outcome: Self-rated hangover effects, ability to function after use, negative and pleasurable effects, paranoia, and duration of effect
magnitude: Mean (SD), synthetic against natural: hangover effects 3.49 (2.80) against 2.79 (2.31), t(854) = 6.45, d = 0.22; ability to function after use 5.47 (2.76) against 6.85 (2.34), d = -0.45; negative effects when high 4.80 (2.89) against 2.80 (2.00), d = 0.64; paranoia 4.75 (3.11) against 3.89 (2.43), d = 0.27; pleasurable effects 4.98 (2.49) against 8.59 (1.70), d = -1.22. Duration: two thirds about 1 h for synthetic, three quarters 2 h or more for natural (Wilcoxon z = -17.82, p<0.001).

evidence.locator: Table 2, hangover effects, ability to function after use, negative effects when high, paranoia and pleasurable effects rows
evidence.extracted: Synthetic against natural cannabis, mean (SD) on 1-10 self-ratings: hangover effects 3.49 (2.80) against 2.79 (2.31), difference 0.70 (3.16), t(854) = 6.45, p<0.001, d = 0.22; ability to function after use 5.47 (2.76) against 6.85 (2.34), t(884) = -13.3, d = -0.45; negative effects when high 4.80 (2.89) against 2.80 (2.00), d = 0.64; paranoia 4.75 (3.11) against 3.89 (2.43), d = 0.27; pleasurable effects when high 4.98 (2.49) against 8.59 (1.70), d = -1.22.

evidence.locator: Fig. 2 (panels A to C); Results 3.5, 1st paragraph
evidence.extracted: When smoked, about 60% reported onset within 5 min for both (z = 1.11, p = 0.268); time to peak shorter for synthetic cannabis (z = -9.44, p<0.001); two thirds reported feeling stoned for only 1 h after a typical joint or bong of synthetic cannabis, while three quarters felt natural cannabis for 2 h or longer (z = -17.82, p<0.001).
evidence.source_read: PDF PDFs/Synthetic-cannabinoids/Winstock_2013_SyntheticVsNaturalGlobalSample.pdf (article in press, not the final version; in-press pages; Fig. 2 checked on the rendered page)

evidence.extracted: Anonymous online survey promoted through Mixmag, The Guardian and social media in November-December 2011; of 14,966 respondents 980 had used synthetic cannabis in the last 12 months, 79.6% male, median age 23. The authors name the self-nominating sample, self-report, unknown composition, polydrug use and recall bias as limitations.
evidence.source_read: PDF PDFs/Synthetic-cannabinoids/Winstock_2013_SyntheticVsNaturalGlobalSample.pdf (article in press, not the final version; in-press pages)

risk_of_bias.note: Self-selected online sample; retrospective, comparative, unvalidated self-ratings that may follow preference (JBI high).

indirectness.note: Perceptions rather than measured after-effects; products of 2011, unknown content.

grade.reasoning: Observational survey evidence starts low; risk of bias -1 and indirectness -1 give very low. The claim reports how respondents compared the two products, not what synthetic cannabinoids do.
